data.title: Hidden Message
data.solution:
import string

def get_character(time):
    minute = int(time.split(":")[1])
    letter_index = minute % 26

    return string.ascii_uppercase[letter_index]


def increment(char):
    next_letter_index = (string.ascii_uppercase.index(char) + 1) % 26

    return string.ascii_uppercase[next_letter_index]


def find_offset(message):
    offset = 0

    while "FRIEND" not in message:
        message = "".join(list(map(increment, message)))
        offset += 1

    return (message, offset)


n = int(input())
initial_message = ""

for i in range(n):
    initial_message += get_character(input())

(final_message, offset) = find_offset(initial_message)

print(offset)
print(final_message)
data.statement:
Your friend lives in a country where the government regularly spies on its citizens. Communication with them is dangerous if they are targeted. In order to circumvent monitoring, you develop a hidden communication system.

Your friend has a social media account where they regularly post innocuous content. When they post, the date and time of the post is displayed underneath it. Using only the time [[HH]]{{:}}[[MM]], each post can be translated into a single letter of the English alphabet. Several posts can be used to communicate a [[message]].

Your friend also decides to use a Caesar cipher [[offset]] for their message. The [[offset]] can have a value between {{1}} and {{25}} <<inclusive>>, and will be the same across all posts. The resulting [[message]] will always contain the substring {{FRIEND}}.

A letter is derived from a post with these steps:

1. Take the minute value ({{00}} - {{59}}) from the post time (the hour component is not used)
2. Modulus that number by {{26}}
3. The resulting number becomes the index for the corresponding letter in the English alphabet:

0 -> A
1 -> B
...
24 -> Y
25 -> Z

Thus, each of the example times below maps to a specific letter:

20:04 -> E
21:01 -> B
21:08 -> I
21:08 -> I
21:11 -> L
22:02 -> C
22:14 -> O
23:05 -> F
00:01 -> B
00:10 -> K
01:00 -> A

The parsed minute values [04,01,08,08,11,02,14,05,01,10,00] from the set of 11 posts above produce the initial string "EBIILCOFBKA".

After the initial string has been produced, advance all characters in the string forward (wrapping around as necessary from {{Z}} to {{A}}) by the same offset until you find the hidden [[message]]. In the example above, using an [[offset]] of <<3>> produces the [[message]] <<HELLOFRIEND>>.

Given a list of [[n]] social media post times, find the correct Caesar cipher [[offset]] used (1 - 25) and the hidden [[message]] it produces.

Optional reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar_cipher

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Your friend lives in a country where the government regularly spies on its citizens. Communication with them is dangerous if they are targeted. In order to circumvent monitoring, you develop a hidden communication system.

Your friend has a social media account where they regularly post innocuous content. When they post, the date and time of the post is displayed underneath it. Using only the time HH:MM, each post can be translated into a single letter of the English alphabet. Several posts can be used to communicate a message.

Your friend also decides to use a Caesar cipher offset for their message. The offset can have a value between 1 and 25 inclusive, and will be the same across all posts. The resulting message will always contain the substring FRIEND.

A letter is derived from a post with these steps:

1. Take the minute value (00 - 59) from the post time (the hour component is not used)
2. Modulus that number by 26
3. The resulting number becomes the index for the corresponding letter in the English alphabet:

0 -> A
1 -> B
...
24 -> Y
25 -> Z

Thus, each of the example times below maps to a specific letter:

20:04 -> E
21:01 -> B
21:08 -> I
21:08 -> I
21:11 -> L
22:02 -> C
22:14 -> O
23:05 -> F
00:01 -> B
00:10 -> K
01:00 -> A

The parsed minute values [04,01,08,08,11,02,14,05,01,10,00] from the set of 11 posts above produce the initial string "EBIILCOFBKA".

After the initial string has been produced, advance all characters in the string forward (wrapping around as necessary from Z to A) by the same offset until you find the hidden message. In the example above, using an offset of 3 produces the message HELLOFRIEND.

Given a list of n social media post times, find the correct Caesar cipher offset used (1 - 25) and the hidden message it produces.

Optional reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar_cipher
Input
Line 1: An integer n for the number of posts
Next n lines: A list of social media post times in the format HH:MM
Output
Line 1: The Caesar cipher offset
Line 2: The hidden message (in uppercase)
Constraints
2 ≤ n ≤ 40
00 ≤ HH ≤ 23
00 ≤ MM ≤ 59
Example
Input
11
20:04
20:27
21:08
21:34
22:37
22:54
23:14
23:31
00:53
01:10
01:26
Output
3
HELLOFRIEND
